title: Diagonal tame chart comparison is a strict closed immersion
statement:
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], with an action of a finite group $G$, and let $\bar x$ be a geometric point with stabilizer $H$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. Suppose there is a finite surjective scheme quotient $q:X\to Y$ with orbit fibres and $\mathcal O_Y=(q_*\mathcal O_X)^G$, and $Y$ is Noetherian. Write $\bar y=q(\bar x)$, $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}=A^H$ using the strict local rings [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and assume $A$ is finite over $B$. Suppose $n=|H|$ is invertible in $A$, $H$ fixes the characteristic monoid $Q$ at $\bar x$, and there is an $H$-equivariant sharp fs chart $a:Q\to M_{\bar x}$ with $h(a(q))=\chi_q(h)a(q)$ for a pairing $\chi:H_{\rm ab}\otimes Q^{\rm gp}\to\mu_n(A)$ and $H$-fixed $n$-th roots of unity. Let $I=(a(q):q\ne0)A$, and suppose $H$ acts trivially on $A/I$. Put $L=\{u\in Q^{\rm gp}:\chi_u(h)=1\text{ for all }h\in H\}$ and $P=Q\cap L$, and let $b:P\to B$ be $p\mapsto a(p)$. Then, etale locally at $\bar x$ and $\bar y$, the charts $a,b$ of $X$ and of the invariant log structure $N=(q_*M)^G$ can be represented on source and target neighbourhoods so that the comparison
$$X'\longrightarrow Y'\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]$$
is a strict closed immersion. Here $X'\to X$ and $Y'\to Y$ are pointed etale neighbourhoods [def-weil-etale-morphism], the displayed target has the log structure from its chart $Q$, and strict means that the log structure of $X'$ is the pullback log structure. On strict localizations the comparison is the spectrum of the surjective ring map
$$B\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q]\longrightarrow A,\qquad b\otimes z^u\longmapsto b\,a(u).$$
Monoid rings and the comparison square are as in [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale], and closed immersion and fibre product are as in [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product]. No log regularity or generic freeness is assumed or concluded.

source.place: Exposé VI Proposition 3.5(b), printed p.74, and proof 3.7(b), diagram (3.b), map (3.c), and Nakayama argument, printed pp.75–76. The cyclotomic coefficient base can be absorbed into the strict chart maps to the integral monoid rings.

proof.text: Work over an affine open neighbourhood of the image of $\bar y$ in $Y$. Its finite inverse image in $X$ is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian, hence Noetherian. The finite-quotient strict-local identification gives $N_{\bar y}=M_{\bar x}^H$, respecting units and structural maps, as well as the assumed $B=A^H$ and finiteness. The strict local rings $A,B$ are strictly henselian local and Noetherian: apply Noetherianity of strict henselization to the Noetherian local rings at the underlying points. Since $H$ fixes the geometric point, it fixes the residue field of $A$: the residue-field embedding into the geometric-point field is injective and commutes with the action.

source.place: Exposé VI proof 3.7(b), diagram (3.b) and map (3.c), printed pp.75–76; Proposition 3.5(b), p.74.

proof.text: Fine-log chart spreading represents the prescribed germ $a$ by a chart on a pointed etale neighbourhood. Pull that neighbourhood back to $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Its image contains the closed point; etale maps are open, and an open subset of a local spectrum containing its closed point is the whole spectrum. Hence this etale map is surjective. The strict-henselian etale-section lemma, with the finite algebra $A$ over itself, gives a section. Pulling back the chart along it represents $a$ on $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Equivariance there is the assumed equality in the geometric stalk.

source.place: Exposé VI proof 3.7(b), diagram (3.b) and map (3.c), printed pp.75–76; Proposition 3.5(b), p.74.

proof.text: The pairing gives $nQ^{\rm gp}\subset L$. Choose monoid generators $q_1,\ldots,q_r$ of $Q$. For any $p\in P$, write its generator coefficients as $nc_i+e_i$, $0\le e_i<n$. The remainder $\sum e_iq_i$ still lies in $L$, because $nQ\subset L$. Thus $P$ is generated by the $nq_i$ and the finitely many remainders lying in $L$. It is integral and sharp as a submonoid of $Q$, and saturated in its group completion: if $mv\in P$ and $v\in P^{\rm gp}$, then $v\in L$, and saturation of $Q$ gives $v\in Q$. Therefore $P$ is fs. For $v\in L$, write $v=u-w$ with $u,w\in Q$; then $v+nw=u+(n-1)w\in P$ and $nw\in P$, so $P^{\rm gp}=L$. At the closed invariant stalk, a fixed section has the unique form $u a(q)$ with $u\in A^\times$. Reducing $h(u)\chi_q(h)=u$ to the residue field forces $\chi_q(h)=1$: if a root $z\in\mu_n(A)$ reduces to 1, then $(z-1)(1+\cdots+z^{n-1})=0$ and the second factor is a unit, so $z=1$. Hence $M_{\bar x}^H=P\oplus B^\times$. This is only a closed-stalk calculation; the neighbourhood chart will be proved below.

source.place: Exposé VI proof 3.7(b), diagram (3.b) and map (3.c), printed pp.75–76; Proposition 3.5(b), p.74.

proof.text: Put $D=B[a(u):u\in Q]\subseteq A$, the image of $\phi:B\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q]\to A$. The relation $a(p)=b(p)$ for $p\in P$ makes $\phi$ well-defined. For $x\in A$, set $R(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{h\in H}h(x)$. The inverse of $n$ is invariant, so $R(x)\in B$. Triviality on $A/I$ gives $x-R(x)=n^{-1}\sum_h(x-h(x))\in I$. Therefore $A=B+I$. This is the source's surjection onto the stratum, proved by the explicit averaging formula.

source.place: Exposé VI proof 3.7(b), diagram (3.b) and map (3.c), printed pp.75–76; Proposition 3.5(b), p.74.

proof.text: Choose nonzero monoid generators $q_1,\ldots,q_r$ of $Q$, with the empty list if $Q=0$. Then $I=(a(q_1),\ldots,a(q_r))A$, since a nonzero monoid element is a sum containing a generator. Each $a(q_i)$ is in $\mathfrak m_A$, since $Q$ identifies with the sharp characteristic at the point. Also $a(q_i)^n=a(nq_i)$ is invariant: each character value has $n$-th power one. Hence $a(q_i)^n\in B\cap\mathfrak m_A=\mathfrak m_B$. Here an invariant element invertible in $A$ has invariant inverse, which proves the equality of maximal ideals by intersection. If $r>0$, take $N=r(n-1)+1$; every product of $N$ generators contains one at least $n$ times, so $I^N\subseteq\mathfrak m_BA$. If $r=0$, $I=0$ and take $N=1$.

source.place: Exposé VI proof 3.7(b), diagram (3.b) and map (3.c), printed pp.75–76; Proposition 3.5(b), p.74.

proof.text: Prove $A=D+I^k$ by induction on $k\ge1$. For $k=1$, use $A=B+I$ and $B\subseteq D$. Write an element of $I^k$ as a finite sum of $k$-fold products of the $a(q_i)$ with coefficients $c\in A$. Write each $c=b+i$ using $A=B+I$. The terms with coefficient $b\in B$ lie in $D$; those with coefficient $i\in I$ lie in $I^{k+1}$. Thus $I^k\subseteq D+I^{k+1}$ and the induction follows. The exponent of Step 5 gives $A=D+\mathfrak m_BA$.

source.place: Exposé VI proof 3.7(b), diagram (3.b) and map (3.c), printed pp.75–76; Proposition 3.5(b), p.74.

proof.text: The image $D$ is a $B$-submodule of the finite $B$-module $A$, and its image in $A/\mathfrak m_BA$ is all of that quotient. The submodule form of local Nakayama gives $D=A$, so $\phi$ is surjective. The finite module in this application is $A$, exactly as assumed in the item; no finiteness of the submodule $D$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 00DV, label lemma-NAK, part (4), with M=A, N=D, the second submodule=A and I=m_B; ILO VI 3.7(b), p.76.

proof.text: By the chart-square construction the strict-local comparison is $\operatorname{Spec}\phi$, whose pullback takes $b\otimes z^u$ to $b\,a(u)$. Surjectivity makes this a closed immersion by the affine characterization. The target has the log structure associated to its chart $Q$. Pulling it back gives the log structure associated to $a:Q\to A$, namely the given log structure on $\operatorname{Spec}A$; hence the comparison is strict.

source.place: Exposé VI proof 3.7(b), diagram (3.b) and map (3.c), printed pp.75–76; Proposition 3.5(b), p.74.

proof.text: First spread a compatible prelog chart, without assuming $N$ is fine. Represent $a$ on a pointed source neighbourhood by fine-log chart spreading. Finite-pointed-piece refinement supplies a finite clopen source piece $X_0$ over an affine pointed etale $Y_0$, mapping to that neighbourhood. Arrange that the pieces are permuted by $G$ as the geometric fibre is: over $\operatorname{Spec}B$ this follows from finite-base strict localization, and the finitely many equalities of their idempotents descend by finite-data descent. The chosen piece is then $H$-stable and the full pullback is the disjoint union of its $G/H$ translates. The finite identities $h(a(q_i))=\chi_{q_i}(h)a(q_i)$ for the chart generators and $h\in H$ hold at its marked stalk. Represent their equality on a common pointed etale neighbourhood and use finite-piece refinement again; the idempotent permutation identities persist under base change. Represent the finitely many root coefficients and their relations on $Y_0$ as well, including inverses of the differences of distinct roots and of $n$. The resulting chart on $X_0$ is diagonal under $H$. On each etale test over $Y_0$, restriction to the chosen piece identifies $G$-invariant sections with $H$-invariant sections. Thus $\mathcal O_{Y_0}=(f_*\mathcal O_{X_0})^H$ and $N|_{Y_0}=(f_*M_{X_0})^H$. In particular the fixed sections $a(p)$ define a prelog map $b:P\to N|_{Y_0}$, with the prescribed germ.

source.place: Exposé VI proof 3.7(b), diagram (3.b) and map (3.c), printed pp.75–76; Proposition 3.5(b), p.74.

proof.text: Write $Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}B_0$, $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}A_0$. Finite-base strict localization identifies $X_0\times_{Y_0}\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A$: the chosen clopen piece contains exactly the chosen geometric-fibre point. Its comparison becomes $\phi$. Choose finite $B_0$-module generators $t_1,\ldots,t_s$ of $A_0$. Surjectivity of $\phi$ gives finite expressions $t_j=\sum_u b_{ju}a(u)$ in $A$, with $b_{ju}\in B$. Represent the finitely many coefficients on a common affine pointed etale refinement of $Y_0$. The differences $t_j-\sum_u b_{ju}a(u)$ have zero geometric germ, so vanish on a common pointed etale neighbourhood of the chosen point of the finite source, by the stalk definition. Apply finite-pointed-piece refinement to that finite source and this neighbourhood. Denote the new affine base and its chosen piece by $Y',X'$. All these identities hold on $X'$. The previous chosen piece has only one point in the marked geometric fibre. Its new chosen clopen piece is H-stable after removing base images of the other pieces: the morphism from each discarded clopen piece to the base is finite, hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], and has closed image by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image]; these images miss the marked point. Thus the quotient and diagonal identities of Step 9 persist.

source.place: Exposé VI proof 3.7(b), diagram (3.b) and map (3.c), printed pp.75–76; Proposition 3.5(b), p.74.

proof.text: The images of the $t_j$ still generate $\Gamma(X',\mathcal O_{X'})$ over $\Gamma(Y',\mathcal O_{Y'})$: scalar extension preserves their generating expressions, and a clopen piece is the quotient by an idempotent ideal, which also preserves them. The identities of Step 10 put these generators in the image of the comparison ring map. It is therefore surjective, so $X'\to Y'\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]$ is a closed immersion. Pullback of its chart $Q$ is $a$ on $X'$, proving strictness as in Step 8. Both structural maps to $X,Y$ are pointed etale neighbourhoods by Steps 9–10. The strict-local ring formula is exactly $\phi$.

source.place: Exposé VI proof 3.7(b), diagram (3.b) and map (3.c), printed pp.75–76; Proposition 3.5(b), p.74.

proof.text: Retain the finite $H$-quotient $f:X'\to Y'$ and its diagonal chart from Steps 9–11. Its ring of functions is generated over that of $Y'$ by the monomials $a(q)$. The action therefore factors, on functions and on the chart log structure, through the finite abelian group $E$ which is the image of $H\to\operatorname{Hom}(Q^{\rm gp},\mu_n(A))$. Its exponent divides $n$. Fix any geometric point $t$ of $X'$ over $s$ of $Y'$, and let $K\le E$ be its stabilizer. Put $F=\{q\in Q:a(q)\text{ is a unit at }t\}$. It is a face. An element of $E$ fixes $t$ exactly when it fixes all nonzero monomial values at $t$, because the monomials generate the algebra over the base. Thus $K=\bigcap_{f\in F}\ker\chi_f$. The chosen root differences are units, so reduction at $t$ does not identify distinct root values. The finite-quotient strict-local identification at $(t,s)$ gives $N_s=M_t^K$ and $(\mathcal O_{X',t}^\times)^K=\mathcal O_{Y',s}^\times$. Passing from $H$ to $E$ discards only an action kernel and does not change these invariants.

source.place: Exposé VI proof 3.7(b), diagram (3.b) and map (3.c), printed pp.75–76; Proposition 3.5(b), p.74.

proof.text: Let $D_F$ be the subgroup of characters of $E$ generated by $\chi_f$ for $f\in F$. Apply finite-character annihilator duality to $E$ with target the original strict local ring $A$. Its root hypotheses hold: $\mu_n(A)$ is cyclic of order $n$; for $e=\exp(E)\mid n$, its $e$-torsion is cyclic with a primitive element obtained by raising a primitive $n$-th root to $n/e$. Any $e$-th root is an $n$-th root. Since $K=D_F^\perp$, the cited duality gives $K^\perp=D_F$. Therefore if $\chi_q$ is trivial on $K$, there are $f_1,f_2\in F$ with $\chi_{q+f_1-f_2}=1$ on $E$. In that case $p=q+f_1+(n-1)f_2$ belongs to $P$ and $p-q\in F$. This is the precise character extension needed at a generization, rather than an inference from the closed stalk alone.

source.place: Exposé VI proof 3.7(b), diagram (3.b) and map (3.c), printed pp.75–76; Proposition 3.5(b), p.74.

proof.text: Every section of $M_t$ is represented by $u a(q)$, $u\in\mathcal O_{X',t}^\times$, $q\in Q$, by the chart definition. If it is $K$-invariant, integrality of the fs log monoid permits cancellation of $a(q)$, so reduction of $h(u)\chi_q(h)=u$ to the residue field forces $\chi_q|_K=1$, since $K$ fixes that residue field and distinct roots remain distinct. Step 13 supplies $p\in P$ with $p=q+f$, $f\in F$. Then $u a(q)=(u/a(f))a(p)$. The new coefficient is a unit and is $K$-fixed because both the section and $a(p)$ are fixed. It belongs to $\mathcal O_{Y',s}^\times$ by Step 12. Consequently the log structure associated to $b:P\to\mathcal O_{Y'}$ maps surjectively to $N$ at every geometric stalk $s$. This includes points whose stabilizer is smaller than the original $H$.

source.place: Exposé VI proof 3.7(b), diagram (3.b) and map (3.c), printed pp.75–76; Proposition 3.5(b), p.74.

proof.text: For injectivity put $F_P=P\cap F$. One has $L\cap F^{\rm gp}=F_P^{\rm gp}$: if $v=f_1-f_2\in L$ with $f_i\in F$, then $v+nf_2=f_1+(n-1)f_2$ and $nf_2$ both lie in $F_P$. If $u a(p)=v a(p')$ in $M_t$ for $p,p'\in P$ and base units $u,v$, the chart by $Q$ gives $p-p'\in F^{\rm gp}$. It lies in $L$ as well, hence in $F_P^{\rm gp}$. Write $p-p'=e_1-e_2$ with $e_i\in F_P$. The associated-log relations for $P$ identify $p$ and $p'$ using the base units $b(e_i)$; the equality of the remaining unit coefficients follows after mapping into the source units, where the base-unit inclusion is injective. Thus the map is also injective on every geometric stalk. Geometric stalks detect isomorphisms of etale sheaves, so $b$ is a chart of the actual invariant log structure $N$ on $Y'$. It is an fs chart by Step 3. This completes the target-chart assertion and, together with Steps 8 and 11, the required strict closed immersion without citing the local Kummer quotient node.

source.place: Exposé VI proof 3.7(b), diagram (3.b) and map (3.c), printed pp.75–76; Proposition 3.5(b), p.74.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q96-77b4ea71d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS, no fixes. Read in full: the item (15 steps, statement unchanged from the Q145 copy) and the new Mathlib leaf; the governance docs incl. delivery-errors A–F; ILO VI 2.3 and 3.4–3.7 (printed pp.73–76, PDF = printed + 6). Source: 3.5(b) states the strict closed immersion and 3.7(b) proves it. Steps 4–7 follow the 3.7(b) argument: averaging gives A = B + I, then I^N ⊂ m_B·A with N = r(n−1)+1, then A = D + I^k by induction, then 00DV Nakayama (submodule clause) on the finite B-module A. Using Z[P], Z[Q] instead of Λ[P], Λ[Q] changes nothing because B contains 1/n and the roots of unity. Steps 9–11 spread the setup étale-locally: idempotent permutation identities hold over Spec B by 05WR/0GIP and descend by finite data; extra pieces are removed by finite ⇒ proper ⇒ closed image; generator expressions descend. Steps 12–15 check that b is a chart of N = (f_*M)^H at every geometric point. At a point t, the stabiliser is K = ∩_{f∈F} ker χ_f (distinct roots have unit differences); the finite-quotient node gives N_s = M_t^K; the duality gives K^⊥ = D_F, which produces p = q + f_1 + (n−1)f_2 ∈ P; injectivity uses L ∩ F^gp = F_P^gp. I re-derived each step.
